top_categories.workout_context: 447 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
36,100ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Raid Pyreneen Randonneur's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
At Raid Pyreneen Randonneur, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
36,100ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
81ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 447 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Road-specific control matters at Raid Pyreneen Randonneur. Practice on paved Pyrenean mountain passes: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 447 miles.
447 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 36,100ft of climbing on paved Pyrenean mountain passes does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Raid Pyreneen Randonneur. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work supports 36,100ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: June in Hendaye (Atlantic) to Cerbere (Mediterranean), France — June-September in the Pyrenees. Valley temperatures 22-27C (72-81F) in summer. Summit temperatures (Tourmalet at 2,115m) can drop to 5-10C even in July. Afternoon thunderstorms are a major risk, building from noon onward with lightning at altitude. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Raid Pyreneen Randonneur. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 447 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 447 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Raid Pyreneen Randonneur. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, VO2max, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 447 miles of paved pyrenean mountain passes in Hendaye (Atlantic) to Cerbere (Mediterranean), France.
